summary: Fortnite is one product with two editors and one server. Fortnite Creative places devices from an in-game inventory; Unreal Editor for Fortnite is a cut-down Unreal Engine 5 that imports FBX, OBJ and glTF, lights with Lumen and Virtual Shadow Maps, and compiles Verse. Everything a creator makes is cooked, validated twice — once locally, once on Epic's servers — and published as a release under an island code. Nothing runs anywhere else and nothing leaves, and that single fact decides most of this map. Three answers here are stronger than any comparable subject's. Scene Graph is a real entity-component scene with prefabs, per-instance overrides and Verse-native components, and it now carries an item and inventory system. The resource budget is a gate rather than advice: memory is computed from cooked data against a bar of 100,000 units and an island over it cannot be published. And agents are shipping — a persona component puts a large language model, named as Google's Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite with ElevenLabs voices, into a character players talk to over voice chat. Four traps for a standards reader. First, two coordinate systems run at once: /Verse.org modules are right-handed Left-Up-Forward, /UnrealEngine.com and /Fortnite.com modules are still left-handed XYZ. Second, the network model is invisible — Verse runs on Epic's dedicated server, and no replication, interest or prediction machinery is published or reachable, so four network rows read empty for a platform that plainly does all four. Third, the player's own body is not a creator artefact: creators author MetaHumans and skeletal meshes for characters in the world, while the avatar stays an account entitlement swapped from the Locker. Fourth, several of the most interesting parts — Scene Graph cameras, Scene Graph animation, custom items — are experimental and cannot be published today. Every geospatial row is out of scope: nothing in Fortnite refers to the Earth.

coverage.note: UEFN draws with Unreal Engine 5's renderer, and the only account of the pipeline given to creators is a performance story: the CPU assembles a manifest, the GPU rasterises and shades it. There is no render graph, no pass order and no shader code; the one authoring surface is the material graph, which does include a post-process material domain. Nanite is on or off per session rather than per creator decision.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Reducing Draw Calls
sources.quote: A draw call is the process of gathering and sending data to the GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) to render part of a frame.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Reducing Draw Calls
sources.quote: Rasterization. It flattens the 3D coordinates to the 2D screen grid.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Reducing Draw Calls
sources.quote: Draw call counts differ vastly between Nanite-enabled sessions and sessions where Nanite is disabled.

coverage.note: No low-level graphics interface is named anywhere in the Fortnite creator documentation, and a creator cannot choose or query one. What is published instead is a quality ladder that stands in for hardware: Low is mobile and performance mode, Medium is Nintendo Switch, High is PC, PS4 and Xbox One, Epic is high-end PC, PS5 and Xbox Series X, with features disabled or scaled down at the lower rungs.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Level of Detail (LOD) Best Practices
sources.quote: The Quality Level Min LOD setting determines the minimum LOD your asset uses at each quality setting. Each of these levels corresponds to a different set of target platforms.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Mobile Optimization
sources.quote: UEFN is designed to handle platform scalability. Due to hardware limitations, some features are disabled or scaled down at lower-quality levels.

coverage.note: Creators author their own materials in a node graph, make instances of them, and can put a material into the post-process domain to filter the whole frame. Material function wrappers let one material carry different behaviour per platform tier. What a material means is Unreal Engine's model, not a published exchange model.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Materials
sources.quote: Creating your own materials and textures in Unreal Editor for Fortnite (UEFN) gives the meshes you use on your island a unique look and feel.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Intro to Post-Processing
sources.quote: Change the Material Domain setting to Post Processing.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Mobile Optimization
sources.quote: Navigate to Fortnite > Materials > Functions, where you will find MF_QualitySwitch_MaterialAttributes, MF_QualitySwitch_Scalar, and MF_QualitySwitch_Vector.

coverage.note: Lighting is dynamic, and that is a platform decision rather than a creator one: Lumen provides global illumination and Virtual Shadow Maps the shadows, and the validation page states plainly that baked lighting cannot coexist with the way Fortnite lights the world.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Lighting
sources.quote: Unreal Editor for Fortnite (UEFN) uses the power of Lumen and Virtual Shadow Maps to create softer shadows, realistic global illumination, and better overall visual experiences.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Validation and Fix-Up Tool
sources.quote: A great example is that Fortnite uses dynamic lighting, and baked lighting would not work in combination.

coverage.note: Post-processing is a placed volume with priority and an unbounded option, carrying colour grading, exposure, chromatic aberration and vignette, and it accepts a creator-authored material in the post-process domain. Epic warns creators that not every device supports every effect.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Intro to Post-Processing
sources.quote: Post processing is a non-destructive way of defining the overall look of the whole or part of an island by using placed volumes in Unreal Editor for Fortnite (UEFN).

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Intro to Post-Processing
sources.quote: PPVs have an impact on the number of variables you have to keep track of for a consistent look throughout the gamut of low-end and high-end devices, as not all devices support all features and post effects.

coverage.note: Detail selection and send order are the same machinery here. World Partition divides an island into grid cells and streams the ones near a player; hierarchical LOD collapses distant groups into one mesh built from the lowest LOD of its parts; per-asset LODs have screen-size thresholds and per-quality-level minimums, and a validator flags a large mesh that has only one LOD.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Streaming and HLODs
sources.quote: World Partition uses Streaming to load grid cells around a player, or streaming source, in and out of memory.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Streaming and HLODs
sources.quote: Hierarchical Level of Detail or HLOD is an optimized grouping of nearby actors where the group is simplified into one static mesh once it is far enough away from the streaming source.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Level of Detail (LOD) Best Practices
sources.quote: The Screen Size value determines how much space on the screen your asset can occupy before the asset drops to a lower level of detail.

coverage.note: Nothing renders Gaussian splats or radiance fields. A title search of the whole 5,525-entry Fortnite documentation table of contents and a full-text search of the documentation return no hit for splat, Gaussian splatting or radiance field, and the closed list of importable 3D formats is FBX, OBJ, glTF and GLB.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Importing Assets
sources.quote: UEFN allows you to import many different file types for different types of assets. While UEFN and Fortnite Creative do not yet support all file formats, this will change over time.

coverage.note: No point clouds, no voxels, no volumetric video. The volumetric-looking tool is Niagara particles, added to a Scene Graph entity as a particle system component, and the importable formats carry meshes and textures only.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Particle System Component
sources.quote: Use the particle_system_component to add Niagara effects to your level.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Importing Assets
sources.quote: UEFN allows you to import many different file types for different types of assets. While UEFN and Fortnite Creative do not yet support all file formats, this will change over time.

coverage.note: Text reaches the world through Unreal Motion Graphics: a UEFN Text Block laid out on a widget canvas, and widgets placed in the world as Scene Graph entities that react to events. Two limits keep this short of native. In-world widgets cannot be interacted with, and a search of the documentation set finds no way to import a font, so typography is whatever Fortnite ships.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: UI Widget Editor
sources.quote: UEFN Text Block: Craft a custom UI message.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: In-World User Widgets Using Scene Graph
sources.quote: You can use User Widget Scene Graph Entities to create UI elements that are reactive to in-game events.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: In-World User Widgets Using Scene Graph
sources.quote: Scene Graph Entities are not compatible with standard devices. To add device functionality, you must use Verse devices.

coverage.note: Viewpoints are bound and blended two ways. Camera devices — first person, fixed angle, fixed point, orbit — are shipping and publishable. The richer model, Scene Graph camera components with a camera director and perspective, orthographic and physically-based projections, is experimental and an island using it cannot be published. The same page carries the platform's clearest statement about where logic lives.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Cameras
sources.quote: Adding a camera to the player's camera_director_component automatically activates the Scene Graph Camera System for that player.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Camera Types
sources.quote: This feature is in an Experimental state so you can try it out, provide feedback, and see what we are planning. You cannot publish a project that uses Scene Graph camera components at this time.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Camera Types
sources.quote: Because Verse logic runs on the server, the FieldOfViewDegrees field is specified as a horizontal field of view assuming a 16:9 aspect ratio.

coverage.note: Scene Graph is a genuine entity-component scene, not a prop list: entities are containers for components or other entities, one simulation entity is the root, and the whole thing is Verse-native so code reaches every part of it. It is in beta and enabled by default in new projects.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Getting Started in Scene Graph
sources.quote: Entities are containers for components or other entities. An empty entity will have no visible effects or functionality. Components are what provide data and behavior to an entity.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Getting Started in Scene Graph
sources.quote: One entity (the simulation entity) sits at the root of your project to represent the simulation.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Scene Graph
sources.quote: Scene Graph is a unified structure that connects all the objects in the world.

coverage.note: The platform runs two coordinate conventions at once and says so. Since release 36.00 the editor and every /Verse.org module transform use Left-Up-Forward, which is right-handed; /UnrealEngine.com and /Fortnite.com module transforms are still the older left-handed XYZ. A creator therefore converts between two handednesses inside one language, and anyone reading a transform out of Fortnite has to ask which module produced it.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Left-Up-Forward Coordinate System
sources.quote: As of 36.00, UEFN uses the LUF coordinate system for the editor and all /Verse.org module transforms. /UnrealEngine.com and /Fortnite.com module transforms use the XYZ coordinate system.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Left-Up-Forward Coordinate System
sources.quote: The change from the previous XYZ and FRU to LUF therefore corresponds to a handedness change in the axes from a left-handed coordinate system (XYZ and FRU) to a right-handed coordinate system (LUF).

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Transforms in Scene Graph
sources.quote: Scene Graph uses /Verse.org/SpatialMath module transforms. Verse module transforms use the right-handed LUF coordinate system.

coverage.note: Content comes in and does not go out. The import side is broad — FBX, OBJ, glTF and GLB for models, eleven image formats, four audio formats, and Epic's own .island and .upack — and a migration tool moves Unreal assets between projects, with the documented directions running Unreal Engine to UEFN and UEFN to UEFN, never the reverse, and brand folders blocked outright. There is no neutral file a second runtime could open.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Importing Assets
sources.quote: There are also two different import options depending on the type of file you’re importing. Importing an FBX file uses the FBX Import Options, all other file types open the Interchange Asset Import options.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Migrating Assets in UEFN and Unreal Engine
sources.quote: Some types of assets can only be migrated one way or not at all depending on the type of content it is. For example, content located in brand intellectual property (IP) folders cannot be migrated at all.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Migrating Assets in UEFN and Unreal Engine
sources.quote: The Migration Tool is a means to move content but does not verify its compatibility with the engine you're migrating to.

coverage.note: Meshes arrive through Unreal's Interchange framework, which parses the file and then runs pipelines over it, with translator settings that convert scene units to centimetres and fix the asset's axis convention on the way in. Triangle budgets are published per asset class, and a Nanite fallback setting decides which triangles count against memory.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Interchange Import System
sources.quote: Convert Scene Unit: Determines whether to convert the scene from FBX units into UE units (centimeters).

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Interchange Import System
sources.quote: Coordinate System Policy: Determines the direction of the asset’s coordinates.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Configuring Collision for a Static Mesh
sources.quote: Use the Nanite Fallback setting to reduce the number of triangles that count toward memory.

coverage.note: Eleven image formats import, and the platform's constraint is unusually explicit: compressed GPU formats must be powers of two on every console, PC and mobile device, and a texture that is not will not stream and may destabilise weaker hardware. Texture groups and mip mapping do the runtime scaling, and mobile guidance caps practical resolution at 512 by 512.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Textures Best Practices
sources.quote: Compressed file formats for graphics processing units (GPUs) must use power of two textures across all consoles, PCs, and mobile.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Mobile Optimization
sources.quote: Texture Groups and Mip Mapping: Enable runtime material scaling via MIP mapping. Ensure textures are in the correct group and created in powers of two for smooth scaling and visual quality. Textures that do not comply with the power of two will not stream.

coverage.note: One sentence in the whole documentation set says MaterialX arrives: the Interchange plugin is described as being used primarily to import textures, MaterialX and glTF, and creators are told not to disable it. Nothing else mentions MaterialX, no page describes what survives the import, and there is no export, so this is an inherited Unreal capability rather than a Fortnite feature.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Interchange Import System
sources.quote: It is NOT recommended to deactivate the full Interchange plugin as it is primarily used to import textures, MaterialX, and glTF.

coverage.note: Animation imports as FBX and becomes an animation sequence the editor and Sequencer replay. The Verse-facing half is newer and gated: with the Scene Graph Animation flag on, every animation asset in a project is exposed as a concrete Verse class that PlaySkeletalAnimation accepts, with ease-in and ease-out windows — and an island using it cannot yet be published.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: MetaHuman Overview
sources.quote: Import an FBX animation of your choice to use with your MetaHuman.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Skeletal Animation in Scene Graph
sources.quote: With the flag on, every animation asset in your project is exposed to Verse as a concrete subclass of skeletal_animation, which is what makes PlaySkeletalAnimation work.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Skeletal Animation in Scene Graph
sources.quote: The Verse APIs described here are subject to change while the feature is experimental, and you currently cannot publish islands that use this feature.

coverage.note: Skeletons are first-class assets with their own editors: a static mesh can be converted into a skeletal mesh with a chosen root bone placement, bone chains are built by hand, and FBX skeletal imports now align the up and forward axes so every imported skeleton faces the same way. The bone naming itself is Unreal's and Fortnite's, published as tutorials rather than as a standard.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Convert a Static Mesh into a Skeletal Mesh
sources.quote: A character's Skeleton Asset consists of a series of bone, or joint chains in a hierarchy.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Left-Up-Forward Coordinate System
sources.quote: Fourth, default imports of skeletal meshes from FBX now use the option to align Up and Forward axes so all imported skeletal meshes face the forward axis.

coverage.note: Nothing in the Fortnite documentation describes importing, storing or driving morph targets or blend shapes, and a full-text search returns no page about them. Facial performance for a MetaHuman is handled the other way round: the animation is baked onto a control rig in Unreal Engine and exported as FBX, and the guide has creators switch the morph export off.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Importing MetaHuman Animations
sources.quote: Right-click on the Face track and select Bake to Control Rig > Face_ControlBoard_CtrlRig. This bakes the MetaHuman animation to the UE Control Rig.

coverage.note: Repetition is cheap and partly automatic: identical meshes with identical materials are merged into fewer draw calls without the creator asking, and instanced and hierarchical instanced static meshes are the recommended way to place many copies.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Reducing Draw Calls
sources.quote: UEFN uses auto-instancing to merge identical meshes with identical materials into fewer draw calls.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Mobile Optimization
sources.quote: Reduce Draw Calls: Avoid rendering too many unique objects and textures simultaneously. Use Instances and Hierarchical Instanced Static Meshes (HISM), and group smaller objects into larger props where feasible.

coverage.note: Prefabs give real layering: a hierarchy of entities saved as a class, nested inside other prefabs, with edits in the prefab editor propagating to every instance and per-instance component overrides marked in the outliner. The older Creative equivalent, the level instance device, behaves the same way for props and structures.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Prefabs and Prefab Instances
sources.quote: Making changes with the Prefab Editor causes all instances to automatically adopt all saved changes.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Prefabs and Prefab Instances
sources.quote: You can override components in a prefab instance to make changes unique to that single instance.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Level Instance Devices
sources.quote: If you edit a copy of the Level Instance device (such as adding or removing props), the change is made to the original and all other copies.

coverage.note: Scale is stated and enforced. One unit is one centimetre, the world grid is 512 centimetres, the up axis is Z, a player character is 192 centimetres tall, and the importer will convert an FBX file's scene units to centimetres for you. This is the clearest units answer of any platform on the map.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Fortnite-Ready Assets Best Practices
sources.quote: In UEFN, the world grid uses centimeters (1 cm = 1 Unreal Unit). When you are creating assets in modeling software or UEFN, make sure the grid size you use is 512 cm (512 units). This is the standard used for Fortnite.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Fortnite-Ready Assets Best Practices
sources.quote: Player characters in Fortnite are 192 cm tall. Keep this in mind when you create architecture or furniture, so that the scale of players fits with the environment you are creating.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Interchange Import System
sources.quote: Convert Scene Unit: Determines whether to convert the scene from FBX units into UE units (centimeters).

coverage.note: Licence terms are collected at publishing time, not carried with the asset. The attribution form has a licence type and licence holder field for each third-party asset, and uploading is a warranty that the creator holds the rights — but Epic explicitly declines to guarantee that the form satisfies any licence, and nothing about permitted use travels with the content, which never leaves Fortnite anyway.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Attribution Screen
sources.quote: Keep in mind that the Attribution screen is provided for developer convenience only. You are responsible for complying with the requirements of any licenses you are a party to, and Epic does not guarantee that the Attribution screen will meet those requirements.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Importing Custom Audio
sources.quote: By uploading content, you confirm that it does not infringe or violate someone else's rights, including their intellectual property rights (such as by infringing another’s copyright or trademark), and that you own or have obtained the necessary rights to share the content.

coverage.note: There is an authorship record and a person types it. Up to fifty attributions, each with content title, source URL, author, licence holder and licence type, are entered by hand and published on the island's details page; beyond fifty, creators link to a web page of their own. Nothing is signed, nothing is machine-readable, and nothing is attached to the asset.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Attribution Screen
sources.quote: You can list up to 50 total attributions.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Attribution Screen
sources.quote: The information and links you provided are added to your project’s island details page on Fortnite.com.

coverage.note: Two different things share the word avatar here, and only one is a creator artefact. Creators can author high-fidelity humans — MetaHuman is free inside UEFN and exports straight into it — but those are non-player characters and props. The player's own body is an account entitlement: an outfit from their Locker, which they swap in game through a Changing Booth device. Nothing about either is portable.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: MetaHuman Overview
sources.quote: MetaHuman, the state-of-the-art system allowing you to create high-fidelity digital humans, is now available and free to use in Unreal Editor for Fortnite!

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: outfit (Fortnite Glossary)
sources.quote: A character's overall appearance is called an outfit in Creative.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Changing Booth Devices
sources.quote: The Changing Booth device lets players access their Locker while a game is in progress.

coverage.note: There are two agreed skeletons and both are Epic's: FN_Mannequin for Fortnite characters and metahuman_base_skel for MetaHumans, and a creator binds imported animation to one of them by name. Neither is published as a bone-naming specification anyone outside could implement, so animation transfers inside Epic's estate and nowhere else.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Transfer Character Animations
sources.quote: As you go through this tutorial, you will practice the retargeting workflows with a Fortnite character using the FN_Mannequin asset inside the Animation Starter template in Unreal Editor for Fortnite (UEFN).

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: MetaHuman Overview
sources.quote: On the FBX Import Options popup, select the metahuman_base_skel from the Skeleton dropdown menu, then click Import All.

coverage.note: No named expression or viseme set appears anywhere in the documentation. Emotes are whole-body actions the player triggers from their own account, and the facial half of a MetaHuman performance is carried as animation baked onto a control rig rather than as named poses a second system could read.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: emote (Fortnite Glossary)
sources.quote: A way of expressing yourself in-game, often as a dance or other movement.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Importing MetaHuman Animations
sources.quote: Right-click on the Face track and select Bake to Control Rig > Face_ControlBoard_CtrlRig. This bakes the MetaHuman animation to the UE Control Rig.

coverage.note: Retargeting is a documented workflow with two assets: an IK Rig characterises a skeletal mesh into limbs and contact points, an IK Retargeter maps one onto another, and the result is new animation assets on the target. Epic is explicit that there is no shortcut — you cannot use a source character's animation on a target without going through it.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Transfer Character Animations
sources.quote: The IK Rig defines the character, while the IK Retargeter defines the mapping for the animation.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Transfer Character Animations
sources.quote: This process creates new animation assets for your target character from the source. You cannot assign animations that are on your source character to your target character without following this process.

coverage.note: Worn things exist in two unconnected places. Simulated clothing is real: Chaos Cloth assets are authored in Unreal Engine 5, imported, and worn by a skeletal mesh in the island. Carried things are item components inside inventories. Neither attaches to the player's own Fortnite outfit, and no attachment-point vocabulary is published for anything to survive a move.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Creating Clothing Assets for UEFN using Unreal Engine
sources.quote: The Unreal Editor for Fortnite supports Unreal Engine's Chaos Cloth Simulation. This system provides accurate and performant cloth simulation for any real-time experience.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Creating Clothing Assets for UEFN using Unreal Engine
sources.quote: You can then import these assets into UEFN and use them in-game with the Chaos Cloth component.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Custom Items and Inventory Overview
sources.quote: Items are created in Scene Graph by placing an item_component on an entity.

coverage.note: No reduced avatar representation is offered to a creator. Every level-of-detail control in the documentation is about static and skeletal mesh assets and hierarchical LOD groups of placed actors; a search finds no crowd, imposter or avatar-quality mechanism, and player counts are capped by island settings instead.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Level of Detail (LOD) Best Practices
sources.quote: Level of Detail (LOD) is important for rendering your asset across different platforms.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Streaming and HLODs
sources.quote: HLODs are generated from the asset's lowest fidelity Level of Detail (LOD).

coverage.note: The avatar is firmly tied to an Epic account, and the account carries state that gates behaviour — a player who declares an age below their country's threshold gets a Cabined Account, and parental controls decide whether they may talk to an AI character at all. What a creator gets is the consequence, not the claim: no account identifier or attribute is published for an island to read.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: cabined account (Fortnite Glossary)
sources.quote: If a player indicates they are under 13 or their country’s age of digital consent, whichever is higher, their account will be a Cabined Account.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: LLM Conversations
sources.quote: We have a parental control to allow voice and written communication with AI Features across Epic Games products.

coverage.note: Rigid bodies work and can be shipped, with the caveat stated in the first paragraph: physics is in beta. Props opt in individually and carry mass, gravity, linear and angular damping and an impulse multiplier. The boundary is sharp and published — Sequencer runs on the server's game thread and cannot interact with the physics thread at all.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Getting Started with Physics
sources.quote: Physics in UEFN is now in Beta. You can now publish projects with physics, but be advised that the tools are still undergoing frequent updates which may affect your UEFN islands.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Getting Started with Physics
sources.quote: Mass lets you determine how heavy the prop is. The heavier the prop, the less impact a force will have on it.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Getting Started with Physics
sources.quote: Sequenced objects run on the server's game thread, which has different properties from the physics thread and does not enact the changes required for physical interaction.

coverage.note: Collision is authored separately from visible geometry and documented in detail: simple against complex, three K-DOP bounding generators, automatic convex decomposition with hull count and vertex limits, combinations of simple shapes, and a collision LOD that only becomes available once the Nanite fallback is on.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Configuring Collision for a Static Mesh
sources.quote: There are two basic types of collision you can set in Unreal Editor for Fortnite (UEFN), simple and complex.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Configuring Collision for a Static Mesh
sources.quote: These options are called the K-DOP simple collision generators. K-DOP is a type of bounding volume where K is the number of axis-aligned planes and DOP stands for discrete oriented polytope.

coverage.note: What is published is not a joint between two bodies but a lock on one. A prop takes rotation and translation constraints that stop it moving along chosen axes, and the page then sends the reader to Unreal Engine's own physical constraint reference rather than documenting hinges or sliders for Fortnite.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Getting Started with Physics
sources.quote: You can add Rotation and Translation constraints to your props to prevent them from moving along certain axes. To learn more about constraints, check out the Physical Constraint Reference in the Unreal Engine documentation.

coverage.note: No surface response model reaches a creator. The physics documentation has no friction, restitution or physical material setting; bounce lives inside named devices — bouncer, pinball bumper, crash pad — and the only tunable is a per-prop impulse multiplier between minus five and five.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Getting Started with Physics
sources.quote: Impulse on Hit Multiplier lets you multiply the force applied to an object when hit. The default is 1, but it can be set to any value between -5 and 5.

coverage.note: The platform never asks two machines to agree, because only one machine simulates: Verse logic runs on Epic's dedicated server and clients are shown the result. The word deterministic appears in the documentation set only as a glossary definition, with no claim that Fortnite is.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: deterministic (Fortnite Glossary)
sources.quote: A deterministic system is one where the same initial state or input will always produce the same results.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Camera Types
sources.quote: Because Verse logic runs on the server, the FieldOfViewDegrees field is specified as a horizontal field of view assuming a 16:9 aspect ratio.

coverage.note: Cloth simulates and nothing else does, and the authoring happens outside the platform: the meshes are made in a package such as Marvelous Designer, converted into a Chaos cloth asset in Unreal Engine 5 with two plugins enabled, then imported and driven by a Chaos Cloth component in UEFN.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Creating Clothing Assets for UEFN using Unreal Engine
sources.quote: The Unreal Editor for Fortnite supports Unreal Engine's Chaos Cloth Simulation. This system provides accurate and performant cloth simulation for any real-time experience.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Create your Clothing Asset in Unreal Engine
sources.quote: Search for then enable the Chaos Cloth Asset and Chaos Cloth Asset Editor plugins.

coverage.note: Regions that fire events are the oldest idea in Fortnite Creative and the best specified: a trigger device relays a signal, and separate switches decide whether players, damage, items, vehicles, creatures, sequencers, water or carried objects set it off, filtered by team and class.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Trigger Devices
sources.quote: When a Trigger device is triggered by a player, vehicle or sequencer, it can send a signal to another device that will initiate a specific action.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Trigger Devices
sources.quote: Determines whether to trigger this channel when the player gets within the proximity of the device.

coverage.note: Sounds are placed and heard by distance. The Audio Player device plays a sound wave or sound cue with attenuation minimum and falloff distances, a linear or logarithmic falloff curve, and a choice of who hears it and from where; sound cues add distance crossfades and a Doppler node; Scene Graph entities take a sound component.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Audio Player Device
sources.quote: Use the Audio Player device to play audio in your project with your own custom sound waves and sound cues.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: Adding Audio to Your Project
sources.quote: A sound cue is an audio asset that runs complex sound design tasks set up inside a node graph.

sources.title: Epic Developer Community: attenuation (Fortnite Glossary)
sources.quote: A change in the strength or volume of a sound. Attenuation is usually tied in to proximity of the listener to the source of the sound, or how close the listener is.

coverage.note: There is spatialisation and there is no spatialisation model. The only control published is a boolean whose whole description is panning by position relative to the listener; the glossary defines spatialisation and 3D audio in general terms, and no page in the documentation set names head-related transfer functions, binaural rendering or ambisonics.

sources.title: Using the Fortnite Data API, Epic Games Fortnite documentation
sources.quote: The Fortnite Data API is a new publicly available API that provides access for developers to key performance metrics from all Epic-made game modes, and eventually for all islands, both Epic-made and developer-made.

sources.title: Using the Fortnite Data API, Epic Games Fortnite documentation
sources.quote: No personal player information is shared through the API. All metrics focus strictly on aggregated engagement data for islands, which maintains player privacy and confidentiality.

coverage.note: A UEFN project is a folder on the creator's own disk that can be zipped whole, Verse source and content included, and a Creative island can be converted into such a project. Missing: Epic states there is no export or package command, the project holds Unreal's own asset files, conversion from Creative is one-way, and nothing is said about what happens if Fortnite closes.

sources.title: Upload Unreal Editor for Fortnite Source to Fab, Fab documentation
sources.quote: A UEFN Source listing contains your whole Unreal Editor for Fortnite (UEFN) project as a .zip file.

sources.title: Upload Unreal Editor for Fortnite Source to Fab, Fab documentation
sources.quote: UEFN has no export or package command, and you can’t publish to Fab from inside the editor. You must create the .zip file yourself from your project folder on your computer.

sources.title: Importing Fortnite Islands into Unreal Editor for Fortnite, Fortnite documentation
sources.quote: Importing a Fortnite island into UEFN creates a fork in the editing access for a project. Once converted to UEFN, a Fortnite island project can only be edited within UEFN, using UEFN tools and features.
